analysis.title: US Macro Snapshot: October Jobs Recap
key_insights: October nonfarm payrolls rose 165k versus expectations of 70k. The prior month's 60k reading was revised up from 29k, and the 3-month moving average rose to 137k.
Natixis says the 137k 3-month average payroll pace is well above most reasonable estimates of the breakeven rate (the job growth needed to keep unemployment stable).
The unemployment rate edged down to 4.14% from 4.17% while labor force participation rose from 61.8% to 61.9%, which Natixis calls an encouraging sign.
On the negative side, the underemployment rate rose and the weeks it takes an unemployed worker to find a job also rose.
Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% m/m and 3.1% y/y, above consensus, and the prior month was revised up. Natixis calls the data noisy and not terribly impressive, with wages subdued for some time.

Natixis prefers wages over payrolls as a gauge of labor market tightness given payroll volatility. Its nominal income proxy and labor tightness indicators suggest little inflationary impulse from the labor market.

Natixis describes the labor market as stable but not hot, and says it is nothing for the Fed to be concerned about. Attention shifts to next week's inflation data, asset markets and financial conditions.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Upside surprise versus consensus of 70k, which supports the view that the labor market is stable.
Upward revision adds to the October beat.
Well above most reasonable estimates of the breakeven rate.
Edged down while participation rose, which Natixis reads as encouraging.
Higher participation means the drop in unemployment came with more people in the labor force.
Above consensus and the prior month was revised up, but Natixis sees wage growth as subdued and noisy.
Natixis says wages show little inflationary impulse from the labor market.

risk_factors: The weeks it takes an unemployed worker to find a job rose.
Jobs and wage data are noisy and volatile, so single prints can mislead.
